text:
More than two child nodes (multi-way split)?
Information gain can be extended to evaluate a split in more than two child nodes
However: the more resulting groups, the larger the information gain (potentially - typically)
Extreme case reasoning:
If you split a parent node in as many child nodes as you have observations
Then each child node will be 100% pure
Then the information gain is maximal and equal to the impurity in the parent node
This is the ‘best possible split’ … or isn’t it?
Cf. supra, infra & Chapter 4 (evaluation – single sample method): more resulting groups =
larger complexity = more risk of overfitting = may hurt generalization power
So: splitting criterion for multi-way splits should ‘punish’ for more groups, to correctly balance
between increased complexity and increased information gain
Detailed discussion on multi-way decision trees is beyond the scope of this course
